newsitem.title: INDONESIA: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 23
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Indonesian newspapers - Jan 23

text.p: The following are the leading stories in the Indonesian press on January 23. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
The Indonesian government will increase the minimum wage in all 27 provinces by an average 10.07 percent from April 1.

Seventy-nine more Indonesian conglomerates have declared support for the government-sponsored programme to develop partnerships with small and medium-sized businesses. The conglomerates will set up a body to organise and coordinate their activities related to the partnership programme.

The government will not withdraw the provisional list of parliamentary candidates drawn up by the government-backed chairman of the Indonesian Democratic Party (PDI), Surjadi, despite protests by his rival. The government has said it will not recognise the PDI under Megawati Sukarnoputri, ousted by Surjadi at a government-sponsored congress last June.

Chairman of the Indonesian Council of Ulemas, Hasan Basri, said he regretted the remarks by an advisor of President Suharto that the recent riots in Tasikmalaya, west Java, were masterminded by the DI/TII Moslem fundamentalist group which was now defunct.
